frictions.title: Small comment upvote target requires repeated clicks
frictions.description: The upvote button on Reddit comments has a small target area under 24x24 CSS pixels, causing the user to perform accidental drag attempts and repeated corrective clicks before successfully upvoting.

interventions.description: Enlarge touch/click target area for comment upvote and downvote buttons.

The upvote control in the comment action row has an activation area under 24x24 CSS pixels. Across two observed occurrences (segment 2376 at 0:18-0:20 and segment 2380 at 0:06-0:13, with matching cursor traces), pointer-down landed on or near the control but slight cursor movement turned the press into a drag rather than an activation, so the vote did not register. The user then issued rapid repeated clicks to correct. Consequence: voting on comments costs several attempts, and users with reduced pointer precision or tremor may fail to complete a routine action at all.
interventions.mitigation: Increase the effective hit area of the comment vote controls to at least 24x24 CSS pixels (for example via added padding or an expanded pseudo-element/inline-size on the button in the comment action row) while keeping the current icon size and visual spacing, and ensure adjacent vote controls remain separated so an enlarged area does not cause mis-votes. Additionally, make activation tolerant of small pointer movement between pointerdown and pointerup so a few pixels of drift still completes the vote instead of being discarded as a drag.

frictions.title: Budget filter slider requires continuous drag interaction
frictions.description: Adjusting the nightly budget filter requires continuously dragging slider handles without an alternative single-click or direct numeric text input method. The user made repeated prolonged dragging attempts to adjust the slider handles.

interventions.description: Expose numeric text input fields alongside the price range slider for direct price entry.

The nightly budget filter on the search results page is adjusted by dragging slider handles, and no equivalent single-pointer alternative (such as numeric entry fields or stepper/preset controls) was observed alongside it. The user attempted the adjustment three separate times with prolonged drags, mid-path releases, and re-grabbing before the value was applied. Users who cannot reliably sustain pointer pressure along a path must repeat the interaction, may set an unintended price range, and can trigger repeated result reloads before reaching the intended filter values.
interventions.mitigation: Provide a non-dragging path to the same result: expose visible minimum and maximum numeric input fields (with associated labels) next to the price range slider, and/or add increment/decrement buttons or discrete price presets. Wire these controls to the underlying range inputs so that committing a value updates the slider state and dispatches the same input/change events the site already uses to refresh results, keeping the slider available for users who prefer it. Also confirm the slider handles are operable via keyboard arrow/Home/End keys and expose current, min, and max values programmatically, and announce the updated result count as a status message.

frictions.title: Repeated adjacent character insertions and backspace corrections during typing
frictions.description: While entering text in Pages, the user repeatedly inserts unintended adjacent characters and extra keypresses, requiring frequent backspace sequences to correct mistakes before proceeding.

interventions.description: While typing continuous prose into the Pages document canvas, the user repeatedly entered characters that were not intended (e.g. stray 'd', 'g', 'bn', '\\' insertions) and then had to issue repeated backspace presses to remove them before continuing. The observed consequence is that a short phrase such as 'fun and re' required many additional keystrokes and repair cycles, so composition speed and effort are dominated by manual character-level correction rather than by writing. The editor did not appear to absorb or offer a low-effort repair for these insertions, leaving the burden of detecting and deleting each stray character entirely on the user's keystroke accuracy.
interventions.mitigation: In the text-entry surface, make error tolerance and repair cheaper rather than relying on precise keystrokes: ensure automatic correction/spelling suggestion for the current word is active and visibly offered inline as text is typed, so a mistyped word can be accepted with one action instead of multiple backspaces; keep those controls discoverable from the editing context rather than buried in preferences. Provide a granular, repeatable undo of the most recent insertion (word-level as well as character-level) that is reachable by keyboard and clearly labelled, and avoid designs where a single unintended keypress triggers commands or formatting changes in the document body. Verify that any typing-assistance state the app owns (autocorrect, spell check, suggestion display) can be turned on per document and persists, and expose the app's own key-repeat/insertion handling settings so repeated or brushed keys do not silently produce duplicate characters.

frictions.title: Pages text entry hampered by unintended key insertions and deletion loops
frictions.description: Text entry in Pages is interrupted by frequent unintended adjacent-key insertions, duplicate characters, and typos, forcing the person to spend substantial effort repeatedly backspacing and re-typing text.

interventions.description: To reduce accidental brief key presses and adjacent-key insertions during typing, turn on Slow Keys in macOS: open System Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard, enable Slow Keys, and adjust the acceptance delay so keypresses must be held intentionally before being accepted.

While composing a sentence in Pages, the observed keystroke stream contained frequent unintended adjacent-key insertions (e.g. 'as' for 'a', 'andf' for 'and') and duplicated characters. The text editor inserted every received keystroke verbatim and provided no observable in-app assistance for these input errors, so the only available recovery was manual backspacing and retyping. Across the session this happened 13 times, repeatedly interrupting composition and making the effort to produce a single short sentence substantially higher than the length of the text would suggest. Consequence: for anyone whose keystrokes are not consistently precise, text entry in the app becomes a cycle of type-detect-delete-retype rather than continuous writing, which increases task time and cognitive load and raises the risk that unnoticed insertions remain in the document.
interventions.mitigation: Reduce the cost of imprecise keystrokes inside the text-entry surface itself rather than relying on the person to notice and repair every character. Concretely: ensure automatic correction and inline spelling/grammar flagging are available and enabled by default for body text, so accidental adjacent-key insertions and duplicated characters are visibly marked and correctable in one action instead of several backspaces; offer an application-level typing-assistance setting that filters implausibly fast repeated presses of the same key and very short keypresses within the editor, discoverable from the app's own preferences and not only from system-wide settings; and make single-error repair cheap and reversible (word-level undo, one-gesture accept/reject of a suggested correction) so a mistaken correction does not force further retyping. Verify these behaviours work when the person is typing continuously, not only after a pause, and that any automatic change is announced to assistive technology so it is not silently applied.

frictions.title: Gmail transient Undo toast auto-dismisses during pointer travel
frictions.description: After deleting an email, the confirmation snackbar with the Undo button auto-dismissed while the user was actively moving the pointer toward it, causing them to miss the interaction window.

interventions.description: Pause or extend display duration of Gmail action confirmation toasts during cursor approach.

After a delete action, the confirmation snackbar containing the only 'Undo' affordance is displayed for a fixed, short duration and dismisses itself without user input. The control is rendered in the bottom-left corner while the triggering control sits in the top toolbar, so reaching it requires a long pointer traversal across the viewport. In the observed session the pointer moved continuously from the toolbar toward the toast between 22.00s and 30.00s, but the toast disappeared at 29.30s and the pointer landed on empty space at (271, 1025). The consequence is that the reversal action for a destructive operation was unreachable: anyone who does not move a pointer quickly across a large distance loses access to Undo entirely, with no alternative path presented at that moment.
interventions.mitigation: Do not tie the availability of the Undo affordance to a fixed auto-dismiss timer. Options that do not depend on unobserved internals: (1) allow the time limit to be extended or turned off via a user-accessible setting, and keep the message visible until dismissed by the user; (2) suspend or reset the dismiss timer while the pointer is over or approaching the toast, or while focus is inside it; (3) place the toast closer to the control that triggered the action, or reserve a persistent 'Undo last action' entry (for example in the toolbar or an accessible status region) that remains available after the transient message disappears. Additionally, ensure the toast is exposed as a status message so its content and the presence of the Undo control are announced when it appears.

frictions.title: Filter controls demand high precision under unsteady pointer control
frictions.description: Filter buttons and drawer menu options have narrow hitboxes that require multi-second corrective pointer alignment, jittery tracking adjustments, and repeated clicks or broken drags under unsteady pointer input.

interventions.description: Enlarge touch and click target areas for PLP filter controls and drawer menu options.

Interactive controls in the product listing filter drawer — size option checkboxes such as 'S', the drawer back button, and the bottom drawer action 'VIEW ITEMS' — present small activation areas that sit close to adjacent controls and drawer edges. In the observed session the user needed multi-second corrective pointer positioning before each activation, and several attempts resulted in repeated clicks or drags that did not register as intended activations. The consequence is that anyone using a pointer with limited precision (tremor, trackpad, head/eye pointer, switch-driven pointer) must spend significant effort per control and risks mis-activating a neighbouring filter or dismissing the drawer instead of applying filters, which can silently change the filter result set.
interventions.mitigation: Increase the effective activation area of filter drawer controls rather than only their visual size: give size swatches, category/filter rows, the drawer back control and the bottom-drawer action button a minimum activation area of at least 24x24 CSS px (targeting 44x44 px where layout allows), for example by adding padding to the clickable element or by extending the hit area with a transparent pseudo-element so visual design is preserved. Ensure adjacent targets keep enough spacing that expanded hit areas do not overlap, keep the label and control in a single clickable region (wrap the size label with its input), and make the primary 'VIEW ITEMS' action a full-width, tall tap target anchored in the drawer footer. Also verify that no filter interaction depends on a drag gesture: provide an equivalent single-pointer click/tap path for any draggable or swipe-dismiss behaviour in the drawer, and activate controls on pointer-up over the target so an unsteady press can be aborted by moving away.

patterns.title: Unsteady pointer kinematics with corrective jitter and overshooting

friction_results.note: GAM surfaced the underlying small-target precision problem and the risk of accidentally activating a neighboring filter, which matches the core unintended-activation friction. It did not explicitly name the CLEAR ALL / VIEW ITEMS adjacency or the missing confirmation/undo.

judge.intervention_note: The produced repair enlarges filter/drawer hit targets, which is a sensible partial mitigation, but it does not implement the expected destructive-action guard (separating CLEAR ALL from VIEW ITEMS, requiring confirmation, and providing undo), so it only partially achieves the intended safeguard.
judge.report_note: The report item mentions small activation areas, mis-activating a neighboring filter, and silent filter-result changes, but it does not identify the specific CLEAR ALL destructive action or recommend confirmation/undo/recovery, so it does not fully cover the expected friction.
judge.pattern_note: Session interaction_patterns explicitly describe unsteady pointer kinematics with jitter and overshooting, matching the expected motor/dexterity input context.
judge.rationale: The motor-precision friction was surfaced with matching severity and the correct mode (repair) was used, but both the repair and the report target general target size rather than the CLEAR ALL adjacency plus missing confirmation/undo, so the intervention and report grades are incomplete.
